Revised assessment: The statement balances solid real activity and strong employment with concern about stalled disinflation, holding the policy rate at 5.25–5.50% and slowing QT. This stance aligns with forecast-based inflation targeting and commitment frameworks that stress waiting for clearer evidence of inflation converging to target (Svensson and Woodford), addresses inflation bias/time-inconsistency concerns by reinforcing credibility around the 2% objective, and is broadly consistent with Taylor-rule prescriptions while inflation remains above target. Under policy uncertainty, a cautious, risk-managed approach (e.g., Soderström; Wieland) supports staying restrictive. The decision to taper Treasury runoff acknowledges balance-sheet and term-premium channels—relevant given the Fed’s sensitivity to the slope of the yield curve and bond yields (Cochrane and Piazzesi). Net tone: mildly hawkish on inflation with a modestly dovish tilt on balance-sheet pace; overall near-neutral but slightly positive given ongoing growth.
